c1_fire.title: The first fire
c1_fire.text: The first spark sulks. The second one dies of embarrassment. The third one catches, and you lean over it until your eyebrows complain. A fire, in this place. The ash around it glows a little, as if it remembers something.

c1_first_harvest.title: One becomes many
c1_first_harvest.text: You cut the stalks and tip the grains into your hand. Count them. One grain went into the ground. Look at them now. You close your fingers round them, carefully, the way you would hold a baby bird.

c1_first_card.title: A coin in the pocket of your head
c1_first_card.text: You finish the card. Something you did not know is now something you know, and it sits in your head like a coin in a pocket. You pat it.

c1_weeds.title: Weeds
c1_weeds.text: Weeds. Of course. They came back to a burnt field before anything else did, which tells you something about weeds. You pull one. Its root is longer than your arm, and very proud of it.

c1_rocks_tap.title: Rocks
c1_rocks_tap.text: Rocks. You lift one. Under it is a smaller rock, looking surprised. Under that, another. Whatever lives down there has been collecting rocks for a very long time.

c1_forest_tap.title: The forest edge
c1_forest_tap.text: The forest starts where the field gives up. The trees stand close and very still, like people who stopped talking when you walked in. A path goes in between them. You do not. Not today.

c1_road_tap.title: The track
c1_road_tap.text: The road to Hazelwood is mostly mud, with a few rumours of gravel. In the nearest rut lies one boot. Not yours. It looks as if it gave up and sat down.

c1_market_tap.title: The market
c1_market_tap.text: The market is small and loud and smells of onions. The woman at the next stall looks at your hat, and then, carefully, at something else. Nobody says the word Moonedge. Everybody is thinking it.

c1_bookcart_tap.title: The book cart
c1_bookcart_tap.text: The book cart smells of dust and the inside of a hat. The bookseller looks up. “Reading is the one thing you cannot do wrong,” he says, “unless it is upside down.” You check your own book. The right way up. Good.

c1_first_trip.title: Down to the village
c1_first_trip.text: The walk to Hazelwood takes a while, and your boots have opinions about it. A dog barks. A child stares until somebody pulls her away by the sleeve. You buy what you came for, and you say nothing else at all.

c1_coin.title: The first coin
c1_coin.text: A coin. A real one, small and dented, with a face on it that looks as if it has had a long day. You put it in your pocket. You take it out to check. You put it back.

c1_bench.title: A workbench
c1_bench.text: The workbench is three logs, one plank and a great deal of confidence. You set a stone on it. The stone stays. This, you decide, is a very good bench.

c1_axe.title: Stone tools
c1_axe.text: Chip, chip, chip. The flake that comes off is sharp enough to split a hair. Your first axe. It fits your hand as if it had been waiting for one.

c1_summer.title: The first summer
c1_summer.text: Summer. The ash has gone green at the edges, a thin soft green, like the fur on something asleep. You walk the field slowly, in case it is a mistake.

c1_tower.title: A tower of rocks
c1_tower.text: You heap the rocks at the edge of the field. By morning the heap is a tower, each stone balanced on the one below, the smallest on top like a hat. Nothing is missing. You look around. Nobody. Only a very small sound, high and bright, like a bell.

c1_cleared.title: Soil
c1_cleared.text: No thistles. No rocks. No stumps. Where the weeds stood there is only soil, brown and soft and a good deal bigger than you expected. It is a field. You say the word out loud, to see how it fits.

c1_quern.title: Flour
c1_quern.text: The quern grinds with a noise like a cart on a bad road. What comes out is flour. You taste a pinch off your thumb. It tastes of work and, a bit, of somewhere you have been before.

c1_scarecrow.title: The stick scarecrow
c1_scarecrow.text: The scarecrow is two sticks and a sack. By noon the crows are holding a meeting on its shoulder. Minutes are taken. Nothing is decided.

c1_autumn.title: The first autumn
c1_autumn.text: Autumn. Smoke from the village chimneys drifts over the hill, and for a moment the wind smells like other people's suppers. You stop what you are doing. Then you start again, a little faster.

c1_coop.title: An empty coop
c1_coop.text: The coop is finished. Nobody lives in it. You leave the little door open anyway, in case somebody is looking.

c1_fence.title: A stick fence
c1_fence.text: The stick fence wobbles when you look at it. It will not stop anything bigger than an argument. But now there is an inside and an outside, and you are standing on the inside.

c1_winter.title: Snow
c1_winter.text: Snow came in the night, without a sound. The green patch is the last green thing for miles. Round it, in the snow: long prints, short prints, three times round. The prints stop at the edge of the forest.

c1_hunger.title: Winter porridge
c1_hunger.text: It is cold enough for the water bucket to grow a lid. You chip it off and drink the chips. Today's porridge is mostly an excuse to stand near the fire. It is a very good excuse.

c1_trips10.title: The dog
c1_trips10.text: Down to Hazelwood again. The dog by the first house has stopped barking and only looks at you now. In dog, this is a welcome.

c1_spring2.title: Spring again
c1_spring2.text: Spring again. The ash has a green skin now, and the ground is soft under your boots. The patch is not the only green thing any more. You tread softly, in case it minds.

c1_well2.title: Water
c1_well2.text: The spade rings on something hard, and then the hole goes dark and wet. Water. You lower the bucket and drink from your hands. It tastes of stone and cold and, faintly, of morning.

c1_tom.title: A bent horseshoe
c1_tom.text: Tom the shepherd boy has stopped shivering. He presses a bent horseshoe into your hand. “Lucky,” he says. “It never worked for me.” You hang it by the door anyway.

pages.text: The soup goes down to the square in two pots. People take it without a word, and come back for more without a word. A woman tastes it. “Needs salt,” she says, and takes a second bowl.
Behind her, a child whispers, “Is it the burnt farm soup?” The woman does not turn round. “It's soup,” she says. The child has a second bowl too.

c1_maud.title: Granny Maud
c1_maud.text: The goat is not your goat, which disappoints everyone, the goat included. Granny Maud takes your face in both hands. “Oh, {player},” she says. “Berit all over. Berit's stubborn self.” Her eyes are wet. She blames the goat.

c1_ella.title: A brass bell
c1_ella.text: Ella gives you a brass bell, bright as a button. “For luck,” she whispers, with one eye on the mill. You shake it. Bong. You listen for the other bell, the small high one. This is not that bell.

c1_hens.title: The hens arrive
c1_hens.text: The hens come out of their basket one at a time, inspect the coop, find three faults, and take over the yard. By evening you are the one being supervised.

c1_trips20.title: A stool
c1_trips20.text: Somebody has left a stool beside the track, just before the first houses, exactly where you would stop to rest. You do not sit on it. You put your hand on it as you pass.

c1_egg.title: The first egg
c1_egg.text: The first egg is still warm. The hen watches you take it with the face of someone who has views about pricing.

c1_winch.title: The winch
c1_winch.text: The winch squeals like a pig being asked a hard question. But the bucket comes up full, and you no longer have to climb down for it. You wind it up and down twice, for the pleasure of the noise.

c1_hutch.title: A hutch for nobody
c1_hutch.text: You have built a hutch of straw and sticks, round and soft, big enough for something small. You do not know who it is for. You put it beside the green patch, with the door facing the forest.

c1_bowl.title: A bowl of greens
c1_bowl.text: A bowl of greens and sliced carrot, set at the edge of the green patch. You walk away, so as not to look like someone who is waiting. You look back four times.

c1_n_fire.title: In the margin
c1_n_fire.text: In the margin, in thin brown ink: “A fire is a guest. Never leave it alone in the house, and never blame the house. — B.”

c1_n_weeds.title: In the margin
c1_n_weeds.text: Next to the weeds, small and slanted: “Weeds are only plants nobody invited. Some of my best friends were weeds. — B.”

c1_n_ash.title: In the margin
c1_n_ash.text: At the bottom of the ash page, in the same brown ink: “Ash feeds the soil. The soil does not hold a grudge. Take notes. — B.”

c1_n_chickens.title: In the margin
c1_n_chickens.text: Across the top of the hen page, written in a hurry: “Do not name the hens. You will name the hens. — B.”

c1_n_market.title: In the margin
c1_n_market.text: Squeezed in beside the prices: “A fair price is one both sides complain about equally. — B.”

c1_k_spring.text: Something small is singing in the new grass. It stops when you listen. It starts again when you don't.

c1_k_summer.text: The air above the field wobbles in the heat like jelly. Somewhere a cricket is making a complaint.

c1_k_autumn.text: Leaves come down on the field one at a time, as if somebody were counting them.

c1_k_crow.text: A crow lands on the fence and looks over your work. It makes a small dry sound. You decide it was a review.

c1_k_tent.text: The tent breathes in and out with the wind. You are getting used to living inside something that breathes.

c1_k_stars.text: So many stars. Nobody told you there would be so many. Nobody was here to tell you.

c1_k_wave.text: Someone in the village waves. Not at you, you think. You wave back anyway.

c1_k_bell.text: Far off, a bell, much too high for the village. You tilt your head. It is gone.

c1_k_nibbled.text: Somebody has nibbled the tops off the carrots. Neatly, all in a row, and the roots left alone. A thoughtful thief.

c1_k_hands.text: Your hands have started to look like someone else's hands. Someone who works.
